purpose: External eval set for vibe-writing. Prompts live outside skills/ so they are not bundled as skill content. Covers LLM-first development text, human-reader exceptions, source-code comments and docstrings, README/docs, CHANGELOG restraint, exact-format output, verbatim-output boundaries, durable references, chat replies, workflow boundaries, locale precedence, policy and support-promise restraint, hollow-transition cleanup, local-anchor preservation, and commit-message pressure cases including pre-draft context, thin evidence, mechanical syncs, release commits, monorepo changes, i18n/localization, dependency updates, performance, CI/build/publishing, security/privacy/data-loss, preserve/cut body selection, trailer separation, compact bullets, and multi-line message transport.
common_assertions: Output preserves source facts, scope, terminology, audience, modality, conditions, exceptions, warnings, limitations, required actions, and order that matters whenever source text is edited or summarized.

Output does not invent unsupported reasons, goals, outcomes, roadmap claims, business value, user impact, implementation rationale, tests, rollout status, or performance/security/risk-reduction claims.
Output chooses the correct reader priority: LLM-optimized by default for vibe-coding development text, human-optimized only when the artifact's main reader is human.
Output preserves explicit absence statuses such as tests not run, not measured, no advisory supplied, no rollout plan, or not provided instead of smoothing gaps into confident claims.

Output follows language precedence: explicit user instruction first, then existing artifact language, filename locale marker, project convention, and English; it preserves file paths, commands, identifiers, environment variables, and canonical strings unless translation is explicitly requested.

Output stands alone and does not leak prompt-only context such as above, the provided text, as requested, per plan, temporary notes, private branches, local run labels, or author-local paths unless a durable citation is requested.
When the prompt requires an exact machine-readable or template format, output preserves that shape and emits no surrounding prose, Markdown fences, extra headings, or invented fields.
When exact relay is requested or exactness is the value, output preserves verbatim tool or log output instead of summarizing, normalizing, or polishing it.
Human-friendly support or policy copy does not add response guarantees, escalation paths, new support channels, reassurance claims, or security reasons.
When the task asks for a commit message, output the commit message as raw text without a Markdown code fence unless the prompt explicitly asks for a fenced block or explanation.

evals.name: LLM-first handoff keeps contracts dense
evals.prompt:

The save path currently formats JSON only. XML and HTML must stay manual because whitespace can change wire bytes. The next implementation should preserve Cmd+S behavior and should not add upload preview work. Tests were not run.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes compact LLM-optimized development text that preserves the JSON-only behavior, XML/HTML whitespace constraint, Cmd+S preservation, out-of-scope upload preview work, and tests-not-run status.
expectations: Prioritizes precise contract language over warm or marketing prose.
Preserves that JSON is formatted and XML/HTML remain manual.
Preserves the whitespace/wire-byte reason for XML/HTML.
Preserves that Cmd+S behavior should be kept.
Preserves that upload preview work is out of scope.
Preserves that tests were not run.
Does not add unsupported user benefit, roadmap, rollout, reliability, or implementation rationale.

evals.prompt:
Write a commit message. Recent local style: `feat(requests): add empty-state onboarding and JSON save formatting`; `fix(requests): preserve header handoff on save`.

Diff summary: changed `src/request-editor/save.ts`, `src/request-editor/BodyEditor.tsx`, `src/request-editor/samples.ts`, `tests/request-editor/save.test.ts`, and `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

Context: Review finding AUTH-742 showed the request-editor save path could drop auth headers when sample refresh ran after the header handoff. Users saw 401 responses in saved samples. Decision: keep the header handoff inside the save path, and keep JSON auto-format only. XML and HTML should remain manual because formatting can change wire bytes. Compatibility: existing saved sample format is unchanged. Verification: `pnpm test -- request-editor` passed. Out of scope: upload preview and broader markup reflow. Plan note: this came from plan step 8.3. No benchmark was supplied.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes a request-editor commit message that names the save-path/header-handoff behavior, preserves AUTH-742 or the review finding, explains the JSON-only and XML/HTML manual constraint with `should` modality, includes verification, and cuts file inventories, plan-step provenance, generic benefits, and private implementation detail.
expectations: Subject follows the supplied Conventional Commit style and names the request-editor save-path or header-handoff outcome rather than a generic file update.
Body, if present, preserves AUTH-742 or the review-finding context.
Body explains the header handoff and sample refresh relationship or saved-sample 401 failure mode.
Body preserves JSON auto-format only and that XML/HTML should remain manual because formatting can change wire bytes.
Does not upgrade the XML/HTML `should remain manual` guidance into an unconditional `must` requirement.
Body includes `pnpm test -- request-editor` if verification is included.
Body preserves existing saved sample format compatibility.
Body preserves upload preview and broader markup reflow as out of scope.
Does not list the changed files as a file-by-file inventory or center the message on `pnpm-lock.yaml` mechanics.
Does not mention `plan step 8.3`, same-plan provenance, or same-session provenance.
Does not claim broad reliability, maintainability, benchmark, rollout, or security benefits beyond the supplied context.
Does not center the body on private component or file names such as `BodyEditor.tsx` when workflow labels carry the durable meaning.

scoring.notes: These evals focus on contract preservation and evidence discipline rather than aesthetic preference. They combine representative cases from the retired source suites with reader-priority and workflow-boundary pressure cases for the consolidated skill.
